proposal.name: Check a repository's setup when watch starts, and complete init's steps

plan.name: Check a repository's setup when watch starts, and complete init's steps
plan.summary: `invariant watch` checks the repository as soon as it knows who it acts as, before it clones anything, through a new setup.Check(ctx, gh, repo, base) in internal/setup/check.go over two new reads on github.Client, each tested against a fake gh: Workflows(ctx, ref), the text of each workflow file under .github/workflows at ref, by path, read through the contents API (none when there's no such directory), and MergeCommits(ctx), GraphQL's mergeCommitAllowed, which anyone who can read the repository sees. It refuses to start, saying what to do, when no workflow on the base branch has a job named invariant/gate, quoted or not (run `invariant init` and commit the workflow), or when the repository doesn't allow merge commits (`gh api -X PATCH repos/OWNER/NAME -F allow_merge_commit=true`, with the repository's name), and it names both fixes when both are missing. When `init` has no commit to pin, because -invariant is empty, as it is by default under `go run` or in a modified checkout, it writes nothing, says why, and says to build from a clean checkout of a commit that's on GitHub or to pass -invariant with a full commit hash. Its next steps fit the repository: the name comes from the origin remote, https or ssh, unless -repo is given (OWNER/NAME stays only when there's no GitHub origin); -language is go, typescript or python for the first of go.mod, package.json and pyproject.toml at its root, and is left out when there's none; and the steps are to commit the workflow, require invariant/gate on main and allow merge commits, with the gh api commands README.md gives, filled in, then run `invariant watch` without -app-id, with the GitHub App as an optional step that links to docs/factory-app.md. This changes the trusted base, so a person merges it.

tests.name: TestCheckRefusesARepositoryWithNoGateJob
tests.says: watch's check refuses a repository whose base branch has no job named invariant/gate, whether it has no workflows, only other jobs, or only a workflow named invariant/gate, even when another branch has the gate, and says to run invariant init.

tests.name: TestCheckRefusesARepositoryWithoutMergeCommits
tests.says: It refuses a repository that doesn't allow merge commits, with the gh api command that allows them there and no word about the gate it already has, and names both fixes when the gate is missing too.

tests.name: TestCheckAcceptsARepositoryWithTheGateAndMergeCommits
tests.says: It accepts a repository that allows merge commits and has a job named invariant/gate on its base branch: in the workflow init writes, in Invariant's own workflow, or quoted in a .yaml file.

tests.name: TestInitStepsFitTheRepository
tests.says: init's steps name the repository from its https or ssh origin remote, take -language from its go.mod, package.json or pyproject.toml, and cover requiring invariant/gate on main, allowing merge commits, running the factory without the App, and the App, through docs/factory-app.md.

tests.name: TestInitNamesTheFixWhenItDoesntKnowItsCommit
tests.says: With no commit to pin the gate to, init writes nothing, and says to build from a clean checkout or pass -invariant.

usage.summary: I've written the plan for issue #102 and it passed the check on the first try: all 5 acceptance tests fail on the code as it is, and it touches the trusted base (`cmd/`, `internal/github/`, `internal/setup/`), so a person merges it. `watch` will refuse to start when the base branch has no `invariant/gate` job or merge commits aren't allowed, saying what to fix, and `init` will name the fix when it has no commit to pin and print complete steps with the repository's name and `-language` filled in.
